data.name: Otto
data.gender_notes: Otto is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Otto is of Germanic origin, derived from Odo, meaning prosperous, wealth or riches. The name has been traditionally given to boys in Christian communities throughout history. The name Otto carries the meaning “Wealth, prosperity” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Otto usually hope their child will grow to embody wealth, prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes abundance, prosperity, and wealth in one's spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Otto belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wealth, prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Otto total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: אוטו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אוטו מקורו בשפה הגרמנית ומשמעותו 'עוצמה רבה, חוזק וגבורה'. השם נגזר מהמילה הגרמנית 'אדאלברט' שפירושה 'אדם זוהר ובעל עוצמה'. לא קיים אזכור ישיר לשם זה בתנ"ך, אך הוא מקושר לנושאים של חוזק וגבורה הנמצאים בכתבי הקודש.

in_greek.name: Όττω
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Όττω προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Ισχυρός, γενναίος και ευγενής'. Η ετυμολογία του ονόματος συνδέεται με το γερμανικό όνομα 'Adalbert', που σημαίνει 'ευγενής και λαμπρός'. Αν και δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Όττω στη Νέα Διαθήκη, οι χριστιανικές αξίες της δύναμης και της γενναιότητας αντανακλώνται στο όνομα.

in_latin.name: Otto
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Otto origine germanicum habet et significat 'fortis, magnanimus et nobilis'. Etymologia nominis Otto coniungitur cum nomine germanico 'Adalbert', quod significat 'nobilis et splendidus'. Quamvis nomen Otto non sit directe in Biblia memoratum, tamen valores christiani fortitudinis et nobilitatis in eo reflectuntur.

in_english.name: Otto
in_english.long_meaning: The name Otto originates from Germanic roots and means 'strong, wealthy, and powerful leader'. Etymologically, it is connected to the Germanic name 'Adalbert', which signifies 'noble and bright'. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name Otto reflects Christian values of strength, nobility, and leadership. Historically, Otto has been a popular name among European royalty and nobility, signifying power and prestige. In modern Christian contexts, Otto is often associated with qualities of courage, determination, and spiritual strength.

data.cultural_impact: The name Otto was often given to the eldest son in medieval European families as a symbol of hope for a prosperous and successful future. It was also a common name for kings, ruling families and noblemen, representing wealth, power, and prestige.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Otto holds spiritual significance as it is derived from Odo, meaning wealth or prosperity from God. Thus, it can be seen as a reminder of God's blessings and a call to use those blessings wisely and for the greater good.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Otto, derived from the Germanic name Odalhari, symbolizes strength and wealth in land, reflecting the ancient Germanic concepts of ownership and protection. Spiritually, it signifies a strong foundation in faith and a deep sense of responsibility toward one's community and possessions.

historical_references.reference: Otto I, the Great (932-973 AD), was the German king who was the first to be crowned as Holy Roman Emperor in 962 AD. He expanded the territory of the Holy Roman Empire and solidified its position as a major political power in Europe.
historical_references.context: German Empire, Holy Roman Empire, European politics

historical_references.reference: Otto III (980-1002 AD), was the Holy Roman Emperor from 983 to 1002 AD. He was a young and brilliant ruler who showed great promise but died at a young age. During his reign, he attempted to centralize imperial authority and expand the empire's territorial holdings, particularly in Italy.
